intro.script: Breaking this morning: AI-found PHP flaws push governments to take websites offline. From the SanMitra Newsroom, this is the Daily AI Brief for 23 October 2026.

stories.headline: AI-found PHP flaws push governments to take websites offline
stories.script: Our lead story today. Two critical flaws in PHP, the language behind more than 70% of websites, prompted a rare NSA warning to patch immediately or take sites offline. Germany, France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Finland and the Czech Republic took some government sites down while patching, and Japan's Prime Minister warned about the risk. The flaws, dubbed PHP2Shell, let an attacker run commands on an unpatched server without a password. They were found with the help of AI models: security firm Calif, working with OpenAI, reported the first in August and Wiz reported the second. The PHP Foundation warned that AI tools now find bugs faster "for defenders and attackers alike". (Themes: technology trends; AI policy and regulation)
stories.whyThisMatters: Two critical flaws in PHP, the language behind more than 70% of websites, prompted a rare NSA warning to patch immediately or take sites offline.
keyPoints: AI-found PHP flaws push governments to take websites offline

stories.headline: Outside evaluators found holes in OpenAI's agent-monitoring system
stories.script: Turning to the United States. The nonprofits METR and Redwood Research said on 22 October that they ran a pilot review of OpenAI's internal misalignment-monitoring system. From 21 July to 11 August, one person from each group had chaperoned, on-site access to OpenAI's codebase and staff. They found several "novel vulnerabilities", including an exploit that would let agents keep "hundreds" of recent actions from being monitored. OpenAI says it has patched the flaws that affected production safeguards. Only a high-level summary is public; a 61-page report went to OpenAI. (Theme: AI policy and regulation) No other genuinely new US model, tool or startup story made the cut in this window.
stories.whyThisMatters: The nonprofits METR and Redwood Research said on 22 October that they ran a pilot review of OpenAI's internal misalignment-monitoring system.
keyPoints: Outside evaluators found holes in OpenAI's agent-monitoring system

stories.headline: Thousands of AI agents read a mouse-brain atlas in 32 minutes
stories.script: Around the world. OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps Research ran thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents in parallel over a whole-brain mouse CRISPR atlas. Each agent took one gene disruption, studied the cell responses, searched the literature and proposed explanations, and the results were merged into a searchable "reasoning atlas". The team estimates the same work would take people months to a year. The agents reproduced human findings and flagged new leads, including a possible link between the Parkinson-like Perry syndrome gene DCTN1 and cholesterol production. In blinded tests, experts preferred these reports 75% of the time. These are hypotheses to test in the lab, not discoveries, and the results are OpenAI's own account. (Theme: AI breakthroughs)
stories.whyThisMatters: OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps Research ran thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents in parallel over a whole-brain mouse CRISPR atlas.
keyPoints: Thousands of AI agents read a mouse-brain atlas in 32 minutes

stories.headline: iFlytek open-sources Spark X2.6, built on Chinese chips
stories.script: In China. At its 1024 developer festival in Beijing, iFlytek released and open-sourced Spark X2.6. It is a mixture-of-experts model with 293 billion total and 30 billion active parameters and a 1-million-token context window, running on a domestic 10,000-card inference cluster. The company says it is the first time coding and agent skills have broken through on fully domestic compute, and that it matches leading systems on several benchmarks. Those are iFlytek's own claims. It also launched a speech foundation model, SparkAudio 1.0. Separately, domestic media report that a Shenzhen team post-trained DeepSeek-V4-Pro on Huawei Ascend 910C chips; that report is not independently confirmed. (Themes: new AI models and tools; technology trends) ---
stories.whyThisMatters: At its 1024 developer festival in Beijing, iFlytek released and open-sourced Spark X2.6.
keyPoints: iFlytek open-sources Spark X2.6, built on Chinese chips

stories.headline: Korea and US air forces sign a pact on AI drone wingmen
stories.script: In Asia. South Korea's Air Force chief Gen. Son Sug-rag and US Air Force chief Gen. Kenneth Wilsbach signed a letter of intent on 22 October on autonomous collaborative platforms. These are AI-enabled unmanned aircraft built to fly alongside crewed jets. The two forces plan to align operating concepts and interoperability for future manned-unmanned combat systems. It is a letter of intent, not a procurement deal. (Themes: AI policy and regulation; technology trends)
stories.whyThisMatters: South Korea's Air Force chief Gen.
keyPoints: Korea and US air forces sign a pact on AI drone wingmen

stories.headline: Chariot launches a real-time speech model for 10 Indian languages
stories.script: Turning to India. Chariot, an AI lab started by former Google DeepMind and Meta FAIR researchers and one of the first four teams picked under the IndiaAI Mission, launched Chariot-1-ASR Realtime. It says the model made 9% fewer errors than Sarvam's Saaras v4 and 26% fewer than Google's Gemini 3.5 Transcribe across 79 public test sets, and 23% fewer than the next-best system in Hindi. These are Chariot's own benchmark results. (Theme: new AI models and tools)
stories.whyThisMatters: Chariot, an AI lab started by former Google DeepMind and Meta FAIR researchers and one of the first four teams picked under the IndiaAI Mission, launched Chariot-1-ASR Realtime.
keyPoints: Chariot launches a real-time speech model for 10 Indian languages

stories.headline: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
stories.script: Around the world. As streaming video generation advances, enabling real-time interaction with generated video is becoming increasingly important. The researchers introduce StreamEval, a unified benchmark for interactive streaming video generation spanning five tasks: avatar dialogue, avatar performance, world generation, instruction editing, and reference editing. StreamEval comprises 300 scripted test cases lasting 15-300s, each specifying initial assets, incrementally arriving multimodal requests, and explicit requirements for state changes and content preservation. Performance is assessed along four evaluation dimensions: task execution, state consistency, visual fidelity, and audiovisual coordination, instantiated through ten task-specific metrics on a 0-100 scale. Evaluating 37 distinct models across 300 test cases, the researchers find that high visual quality and identity retention do not necessarily coincide with reliable request execution or sustained state consistency.
stories.whyThisMatters: As streaming video generation advances, enabling real-time interaction with generated video is becoming increasingly important.
keyPoints: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models

stories.headline: Singapore opens a national embodied-AI challenge for chip factories
stories.script: In Asia. ASTAR, the National Robotics Program, PINE Lab@NTU and Micron launched the Singapore Embodied AI Challenge for Manufacturing. Teams worldwide will program robots to open, service, inspect and reassemble a mock semiconductor chamber, with S88,000 dollars in prizes. A simulation round runs until 31 December, and the finals are at RoboSG! on 20 March 2027. (Theme: technology trends) ---
stories.whyThisMatters: A*STAR, the National Robotics Program, PINE Lab@NTU and Micron launched the Singapore Embodied AI Challenge for Manufacturing.
keyPoints: Singapore opens a national embodied-AI challenge for chip factories

stories.headline: Karta AI raises 3 million dollars to automate bank and lender support calls
stories.script: Turning to India. Karta AI, founded by former Razorpay executives, raised a 3 million dollars seed round led by PeerCapital and Cedar Hill Capital. It builds voice agents for complex inbound calls at banks, lenders and insurers, and names PhonePe, Pine Labs, Bajaj and Aavas as customers. The company says its agent resolves about 70% of borrower queries without a human. That figure is the company's own claim. (Theme: AI industry and startup news) No new national AI policy move in India made the cut in this window.
